 Oregon prioritizes prosecution of SNAP fraud cases amid millions in stolen benefits 
 The Oregon Department of Justice says it has been directed by the White House to prioritize prosecuting cases of SNAP fraud. By Julia Lopez Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 6:06 PM PDT | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The Oregon Department of Justice says it has been directed by the White House to prioritize prosecuting cases of SNAP fraud. 
 Since October 2024, the federal government says more than $3 million in food assistance funds has been stolen in Oregon, and officials have filed nearly a dozen new indictments.
 More than 700,000 people in Oregon rely on SNAP benefits, according to federal data. That accounts for 18% of the state population.
 Devices used to steal benefit data have been found at convenience and grocery stores across the state. Department of Justice attorney Scott Bradford said it is easy to target EBT cards because Oregon’s cards are not chipped. Participants could swipe their cards, have their data stolen, and find a zero balance the next time they go shopping.
 In the past two months, Bradford said the DOJ has filed 11 new indictments for $143,000 in stolen EBT funds. The funds were used to buy baby formula and energy drinks that are sold for cash on the black market.
 “Over the past year we have taken apart criminal operations that use skimming devices, stolen card data and coordinated theft rings to syphon benefits meant for Oregonians simply trying to put food on the table,” said Scott Bradford, U.S. district attorney for Oregon. “These schemes aren’t small. They are organized and deliberate and widespread and we are dismantling them piece by piece.”
 Bradford said the DOJ is investigating whether any stores have been involved in the schemes. The schemes were uncovered in October 2024, when $2.4 million in stolen funds were discovered. Since then, more than two dozen people involved in two theft rings have been charged or sentenced. Bradford said he is unclear if any funds have been returned to victims of fraud.
 Sen. Ron Wyden has introduced a bipartisan bill that would require states to issue SNAP cards with chips to increase security.
